commit_message:
[feat](prism): per-expert variable K geometry and gather-to-dense

Implements the kt half of band-to-index (K3+K4 of the plan, merged because they
are one change: in index mode idx always accompanies row_off, so the gather is
not separable from the geometry).

KIndex has exactly two modes. Empty row_off means the degenerate case -- one
shared contiguous band, the byte-identical path we had -- and a populated row_off
always arrives with idx. A third mode for "contiguous but variable" would save
two bytes per row and cost a branch in every gather site, which is a bad trade.

The no-argument accessors are gone rather than kept alongside. gateup_k() splits
into gateup_k(e) and gateup_k_max(), so the compiler asks at all 44 call sites
whether that position is per-expert or a worst case; getting it wrong under
variable K is a silent wrong answer, not a crash. The classification turned out
mechanical: pool sizes take the max, everything else is per-expert.

One thing had to be split that I initially conflated. A single helper returned
"a dense pointer, zero-copy when degenerate", which is right for decode and wrong
for prefill, where each token must land in its own slot. Prefill silently packed
an untouched buffer; seven tests caught it. There are now two: gather_rows always
writes to dst, dense_rows returns a pointer and only copies when indexed.

The gather destination reuses m_local_input_, which has no other consumer during
the decode gateup phase, so the addition costs no memory. The mask builder reads
the same buffer, which is what keeps the mask bit to packed tile correspondence
intact: the packed row order is the gathered order.

Score-table offsets move from e*rows to row_base(e), and pair_dot to half that --
even by construction, since every k(e) is a multiple of K_STEP. TP staging moves
the same way, with per-expert element counts and row_base for both the source and
the node-local destination.

init validates what would otherwise fail silently: row_off monotone, idx length
agreeing with it, per-expert rows a multiple of K_STEP (the plan-level rule is
only the pair, and rounding up to the tile is the loader's job), and indices
inside the axis. The last two are the difference between a hard error and reading
another expert's columns.

Tests: the existing band suite stays bit-exact (23 passed unchanged), and nine
new ones cover what bands cannot express -- variable k[e], shuffled indices, the
contiguous index matching the band path bitwise, and integer bit-exactness under
shuffling, which is the only exact detector of coordinate scrambling. Under a
band that test verifies nothing about order, since any order sums the same rows.
